You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Oriole Festival setup","question":"Can operations close the sign-off for the west entrance count?","claims":{"A":"West entrance had zero ticket scans in the first minute.","B":"At least six ushers were present at the west entrance at 09:00.","C":"West entrance opened at 09:00."},"handoff":"The case concerns whether operations can close the sign-off for the west entrance at the Oriole Festival setup. The prior assessment found Claim A (zero ticket scans in the first minute) contradicted by gate log S3 showing eight scans, so the entrance was active immediately. Claim C (west entrance opened at 09:00) is well supported by duty log S1. Claim B (six ushers present at 09:00) remains unresolved due to lack of sign-in records, despite the roster assigning six ushers and the coordinator’s assumption of attendance. The key evidence supports that the entrance was open and operational with ticket scans, but usher presence is uncertain. This suggests sign-off can proceed based on entrance activity, though usher attendance is not fully verified.","follow_up":{"S4":"an independent opening-time photograph and vest-code roster verify six ushers at West entrance at 09:00."}}

Claim C is well supported by duty log S1 confirming the west entrance opened at 09:00. Claim B was previously unresolved due to lack of sign-in records, but follow-up source S4 independently verifies six ushers present at 09:00 via photograph and roster, supporting the claim. Thus, the evidence decisively supports that the west entrance opened on time with active ticket scanning and sufficient usher presence, allowing operations to close the sign-off."}

parsed.note: Claim A is contradicted by gate log S3 showing eight ticket scans in the first minute, proving the entrance was active immediately. Claim C is well supported by duty log S1 confirming the west entrance opened at 09:00. Claim B was previously unresolved due to lack of sign-in records, but follow-up source S4 independently verifies six ushers present at 09:00 via photograph and roster, supporting the claim. Thus, the evidence decisively supports that the west entrance opened on time with active ticket scanning and sufficient usher presence, allowing operations to close the sign-off.
